claim: FACTSCORE decomposes a long-form LLM generation into atomic facts and computes the percentage of atomic facts supported by a reliable knowledge source, solving the problem that binary factual/non-factual judgments are inadequate for mixed-support generations.
stance_target: pillar 1: granular, decomposed factuality evaluation methodology for rigid evals
scope_conditions: long-form text generation evaluation, people biographies domain tested
quoted_support: we introduce FACTSCORE, a new evaluation that breaks a generation into a series of atomic facts and computes the percentage of atomic facts supported by a reliable knowledge source.
time_period: 2023 (original publication), relevant as a 2026 cited benchmark

claim: ChatGPT achieves only a 58% human-evaluated FACTSCORE on generated people biographies, demonstrating the need for fine-grained factuality scoring rather than binary correctness judgments.
stance_target: pillar 1: LLM factuality is partial even for state-of-the-art commercial models, justifying rigid evals
scope_conditions: human evaluation of biography generation task, 2023 study
quoted_support: we report new analysis demonstrating the need for such a fine-grained score (e.g., ChatGPT only achieves 58%).

claim: An automated FACTSCORE estimator using retrieval and a strong LLM judge achieves less than a 2% error rate compared to costly human evaluation, and applying it to 6,500 generations from 13 recent LMs would have cost $26,000 if done by human annotators.
stance_target: pillar 6: cost optimization — automated LLM-judge evaluation is dramatically cheaper than human evaluation at comparable accuracy
scope_conditions: automated vs. human factuality evaluation comparison, 13 LMs, 6,500 generations
quoted_support: we also introduce an automated model that estimates FACTSCORE using retrieval and a strong language model, with less than a 2% error rate. Finally, we use this automated metric to evaluate 6,500 generations from a new set of 13 recent LMs that would have cost $26K if evaluated by humans.

claim: GPT-4 and ChatGPT are measurably more factual than public open-source models, with Vicuna and Alpaca ranking among the best public models by FACTSCORE.
stance_target: comparative factuality benchmarking of commercial vs open models
quoted_support: GPT-4 and ChatGPT are more factual than public models, and Vicuna and Alpaca are some of the best public models.
